author: Rdk123
text:
Anyone watching my brent and WTI charts, the brent zone to watch held well as a great demand and it was clear to see how these lower time frame zones really get respected (dotted lines roughly show the zones but decisions on price defines them, this is how I'm using them now anyway).

WTI wanted lower in to the FO zone below the D1 QM, it's found demand right at the base of the daily low from march. If you zoom in to that low you'll see that it has reacted at a lovely M15/H1/H4 QM level, right where the imbalance occurred, price was deemed far too cheap as the buyers massively outweighed the sellers and pushed price up 4 dollars or so in no time at all. It has taken over a week to get down from 46 dollars and about an hour of trading time to get back there from 42. Unless someone is really hell bent on taking oil in general lower I would like to think we would have a reaction here. As OIL is so volatile at the minute it's best to jsut watch PA unfold.

Rdk123 wrote: Did anyone catch this from my post on Friday?? Lovely PA on the M5 today at the D1 QM level, could be part of a bigger move upwards.

Price engulfs North, orders removed from the edge of the CP zone, RT back to demand on the edge, small CP in to demand, price is then clear to run all of the way up to 44.81.

Best to just keep an eye on pa from here.

Same with brent;

Rdk123 wrote: WTI D1, QM level, maybe wait for LTF confirmation? Could be an excellent area for a long. What do you think? If there is some news over the weekend that could influence OIL prices then this could be a good shout.

Brent is also at demand. Worth keeping an eye on.

author: Rdk123
text:
Cheers Josh, not trading at the minute because i can't commit the time to sit and watch. I do try and mark up charts each evening though to see how price has been moving and whether it has done so in the way I thought it would.

I also listened to a trader on one of those 'periscope' cam things last night. He had some very good lessons for aspiring traders, irrelevant of the method.

One of the key things went something like this 'assimilate, imitate and innovate', This is priceless advice, we must not be scared to push the boundaries of what we already know, we have nothing to lose by testing theories built on knowledge of tried and tested methods to improve our understanding.

RTM leaves so much room to innovate it's unreal, this is shown in the multiple different ways many traders trade here, using the same principles. We are not all the same and we need to adapt to our strengths and what we are comfortable with. If we can approach trading from a position of strength, rather than weakness, then we are already one step ahead of the game.

text: New colour scheme and quick trade this morning. GBPUSD. This A to B trade sums up pretty much How I want to trade. This could be the start of the bigger move down but I am not happy with price coming back at me. I would rather take profit and the first sensible target and then look for the next OP. If that mean taking the next leg down on the same move then so be it, but at least I'm not watching the painful ups when I'm only interested in the downs!
